Good news — most of the plumbing is already in the tree, just disabled. Here's what I found and a phased plan.

## What already exists on `development`

- **Upload screen** [log_viewer.cpp](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/log_viewer.cpp) (295 lines) — has a working `ChunkedHTTPClient` that POSTs multipart/form-data to `API_LOGFILE_ENDPOINT` ([log_viewer.cpp:199-294](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/log_viewer.cpp#L199-L294)). Connects WiFi on enter, disconnects on leave.
- **File browser** [file_browser.cpp](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/file_browser.cpp) (406 lines) — enumerates SD files with pagination + a "mark for upload" UI hook.
- **API endpoint** `API_LOGFILE_ENDPOINT = http://api.safecast.org/bgeigie_imports.json` defined in [user_config.h:108](bgeigiezen_firmware/user_config.h#L108).
- **WiFi connect/disconnect helpers**, dual-profile credential storage, and a config web server — already in place.
- **Menu entry exists but is disabled:** [menu_window.cpp:19](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/menu_window.cpp#L19) — `{.title="Log viewer", .tooltip="Log viewer (in progress)", .enabled=false, ...}`.

So what you started is checked into `development` already, just turned off. Last work on it was a `wip log viewer` commit. The "different branch from a month ago" you remember — was it perhaps merged into `development` and then disabled? Worth confirming. (If you remember the branch name, I can diff it.)

## Concrete gaps before this can ship

1. Filename is hardcoded — `"2024-11-30_1227.log"` at [log_viewer.cpp:245](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/log_viewer.cpp#L245) instead of `_detail_log_file_name`.
2. File selector not wired — `// TODO: selector down` comments, no integration with `FileBrowserScreen`.
3. No upload progress UI / no success/error feedback to the user — POST happens, response is only logged via `M5_LOGD`.
4. No retry / resume / "already uploaded" tracking — re-tapping Upload would re-POST.
5. The menu entry is `enabled=false` — needs flipping plus a tested path.
6. HTTPS not used — endpoint is `http://`. Safecast API supports https; worth deciding.
7. `Host` header is set to `TTSERVE_HOST` ([log_viewer.cpp:227](bgeigiezen_firmware/screens/log_viewer.cpp#L227)) but the URL points at `api.safecast.org` — that's a bug.

## Proposed phased plan

**Phase 1 — Make a single manual upload work end-to-end (smallest viable slice)**
- Fix the hardcoded filename and `Host` header bugs.
- Wire `FileBrowserScreen` → `LogViewerScreen` so the user picks a file, then presses Upload.
- Show on-screen status: `Connecting WiFi → Uploading X% → Done / HTTP <code>`.
- Flip the menu entry to `enabled=true` only when WiFi creds and API key are present.
- **Test on a real device** with a small log file against the real API (with your account's API key).

**Phase 2 — Robustness**
- Switch to HTTPS (`WiFiClientSecure`) and add the Safecast cert/CA bundle (or use `setInsecure()` as a first cut, document the trade-off).
- Track uploaded filenames in a `.uploaded` sidecar file or `LocalStorage` so the same log isn't re-sent. Show a checkmark in the file browser.
- Handle response codes properly: parse JSON for `id` (the upload ID) on success; surface error messages.
- Sane chunk size / yield to watchdog on long uploads.

**Phase 3 — Convenience (optional)**
- "Upload all unsent" action.
- Auto-upload on WiFi-connect option in settings.
- Progress bar + cancel button.

## Questions before I commit to anything

1. Do you want me to **continue from the existing `log_viewer.cpp`** (recommended — it's most of the way there) or start a fresh `feature/sd-upload` branch from `development`?
2. Do you remember the older branch name? If it has work that didn't make it into `development`, I'll cherry-pick.
3. HTTPS now or later? (Affects Phase 1 scope.)
4. Where should the API key come from — existing `LocalStorage::get_api_key()` is already referenced; is that field exposed in the settings menu yet, or does that also need wiring?

If Phase 1 as scoped above sounds right, say the word and I'll start with the filename/Host bug fixes and the file-browser → log-viewer wiring.
